title: Error Budget Orchestration & Cutover Plan — Q3 2026
content:
Executive summary:

This doc lays out a cross-functional program to operationalize error budget orchestration across Redwood services and execute a coordinated cutover from the existing ad-hoc oncall/incident reaction model to an SLO-driven reliability regime. The plan covers policy, runbooks, automation, pilot, and org-wide cutover. Core outcome: teams treat error budget as a first-class signal (deploy gating, routing, and engagement) with automated enforcement where appropriate, and a simple, low-friction escalation model during budget exhaustion.

Why now:
- Growing customer use of low-latency endpoints requires predictable availability and defined tradeoffs (cost vs. latency).
- We lack a consistent, cross-team way to translate SLO violations into operational actions (e.g., slow rollouts, traffic shedding, prioritized bug fixes).
- Incidents are still handled largely by tribal knowledge; we need standardized runbooks and automation to reduce MTTD/MTTR.

Goals (measurable):
- Within 12 weeks, 80% of critical public-facing services have formal SLOs and associated runbooks documented in Confluence.
- Reduce mean incident-to-first-response time for SLO-related alerts by 50% in pilot teams.
- Implement error-budget-aware deployment gating for 3 high-traffic services and demonstrate reduced post-deploy regressions.
- Establish a cadence: weekly error-budget review digest + monthly reliability scorecard per service.

Scope (what's in / out):
In scope:
- Public API services (hosted-api) and the serving runtime control plane (serving-runtime).
- Observability pipelines (Datadog + internal metrics ingestion) and PagerDuty integration.
- Runbook templates, enforcement automation, deployment gating logic, and communication playbooks.
Out of scope:
- Deep instrumentation work that requires model-internal tracing (to be scheduled separately).
- Long-term SLA commercial changes (legal/product will handle later).

Stakeholders and roles:
- Program lead: Aisha Patel (eng-sre) — owns timeline, cross-team coordination, cutover decision.
- Observability lead: Marcus Lin (observability) — metrics ingestion, dashboards, alerting rules.
- Serving runtime: Sofia Martinez (serving-runtime) — SLO definitions for generation and chat endpoints, KV cache considerations.
- Hosted API product: Priya Nair (product-hosted-api) — prioritization of customer-impact services and communication to customers.
- Platform infra: Ethan Cole (infrastructure) — deployment gating hooks, circuit breakers at routing layer.
- Oncall and tooling: Benji Park (site-reliability-engineering) — PagerDuty taxonomy, escalation flows.

High-level timeline (12-week plan):
Phase 0 — Prep (week 0–1): assemble team, finalize pilot services, baseline metrics.
Phase 1 — Policy & SLO drafting (week 2–3): define SLI sources, SLO windows (30d/7d), error budget math, burn thresholds.
Phase 2 — Runbooks & Playbooks (week 4–5): author runbooks, create incident-to-action mapping for burn states.
Phase 3 — Automation & Integrations (week 6–8): implement alert hooks, PagerDuty playbooks, deployment gating in CI/CD.
Phase 4 — Pilot & Iterate (week 9–10): run 3-week pilot on selected services, capture metrics, tweak thresholds.
Phase 5 — Org cutover (week 11–12): expand to other teams, training sessions, formal handoff and retrospective.

Milestones and deliverables (per phase):
- Prep: pilot roster, baseline dashboards, inventory of SLIs for each pilot service.
- Policy & SLOs: SLO document per service (owner, SLI definition, target, window), policy matrix that maps burn to actions.
- Runbooks: templated runbooks in Confluence, runbook for error-budget exhaustion with specific scripts and contact points.
- Automation: alert rules in Datadog, PagerDuty escalation playbooks, CI/CD gate PR templates, traffic routing playbooks.
- Pilot review: quantitative pilot report (deploy regression rate, response times, false positives).
- Cutover package: training slides, quick reference cards, oncall rotation updates.

Detailed tasks by team:
- Observability (Marcus):
  - Map existing metrics to canonical SLIs (latency p95/p99, error-rate by error-class, availability).
  - Create Datadog composite SLO objects where possible, export to internal metrics index.
  - Build SLO dashboards and weekly digest email templates.
- Serving Runtime (Sofia):
  - Propose SLOs for generation endpoints (token-level vs request-level decisions).
  - Document how prefix/KV cache behavior affects SLI calculations and add tags to metrics for cache-hit vs miss.
  - Add optional debug flags to emit per-request SLO attribution for first pilot.
- Hosted API Product (Priya):
  - Select three pilot routes (high traffic, prototypical failure modes).
  - Define customer communication templates for when we engage in mitigation (rate limits, degraded mode).
- Platform Infra (Ethan):
  - Implement a lightweight deployment gate hook: block canary promotion when error budget < X% (configurable).
  - Implement traffic-weighted fallback policy that can route to a lower-capacity but higher-stability model variant.
- Oncall/Tools (Benji):
  - Design PagerDuty service categories and escalation policies tied to SLO burn levels.
  - Create runbook-triggered automation (e.g., slack notify + runbook link + ephemeral incident channel).

Runbook: Error Budget Exhaustion (template snippet)
- Trigger: composite SLO alert (7d burn > 20% or 1h instantaneous burn > 5%).
- Immediate actions (first 15 mins):
  1) PagerDuty page owner for the SLO.
  2) Post ephemeral incident channel in #sre-reliability and tag product owner.
  3) Check Datadog dashboard for recent deploys (last 60m), traffic spikes, and external dependencies.
- Mitigations (first 60 mins):
  - If recent deploy suspected: initiate rollback or pause the pipeline (CI gate).
  - If traffic spike: engage routing team to apply traffic shaping or priority queues.
  - If external dependency: engage vendor/partner and enable degrade mode per product guidance.
- Restore and postmortem:
  - When SLO recovers (below warning threshold for 1h), close incident and create a short postmortem, tag "SLO-impact".

Automation & CI/CD gating specifics:
- Implementation pattern: a lightweight API from infra exposes current error budget percentage per service. CI/CD pipeline can query this API before promoting canary. Default allow threshold = 30% (configurable by service owner).
- Rollout plan: pilot services set threshold to 20% for testing, logs written to audit stream.
- Safety: gating should only block auto-promotions; manual overrides allowed with mandatory incident log entry.

Pilot selection criteria and chosen services:
- Criteria: high traffic, clear SLI instrumentation, active oncall owner, different failure modes (latency vs error-rate).
- Chosen pilots:
  1) hosted-api/v1/generate (latency-affected, high qps) — owner: Priya Nair
  2) serving-runtime/control-plane (route and model selection latency) — owner: Sofia Martinez
  3) embeddings-service (lower latency but sensitive to OOMs) — owner: Ethan Cole

Metrics and KPIs to track during pilot:
- Incident-to-first-response (minutes)
- Mean time to mitigation (minutes)
- Post-deploy regression rate (percent of deploys with SLO blips)
- False positive alert rate (alerts not leading to actionable state)
- Error budget consumption rate (daily burn %)

Communication plan:
- Weekly: short reliability digest to eng-all with top 5 services and their burn status.
- Ad-hoc: when any service crosses critical burn threshold, auto post to #sre-reliability and an email to product stakeholders.
- Training: two 60-minute training sessions for pilot teams on runbooks and CI gating; office hours for broader teams.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Alert fatigue if thresholds too low -> Mitigation: tune thresholds in pilot, adjust alert severity and suppress noisy signals at SLI level.
- Risk: Teams bypass gating via manual overrides -> Mitigation: require incident ticket and post-override review.
- Risk: Ownership ambiguity across platform/product -> Mitigation: signed owner list and SLA for corrective actions in the policy document.

Open decisions (for program council):
- Should we enforce gating on all internal deploys or only auto-promotions? (proposal: auto-promotions only)
- Burn threshold defaults: 20% vs 30% — pilot will use 20% and we will evaluate.
- Which SLO window should be primary: 7d rolling for burn sensitivity vs 30d for contractual view? (proposal: use both; 7d for ops, 30d for reporting)

Acceptance criteria for org cutover:
- >= 80% of services with SLOs have an associated runbook and PagerDuty category.
- CI gating implemented for at least 3 services with audit logs enabled.
- Oncall teams demonstrate <50% of current incident-to-first-response time in pilot.

Next steps (week-by-week immediate):
Week 0: finalize pilot roster, create baseline dashboards (Marcus).
Week 1: host cross-team kickoff, distribute owner responsibilities (Aisha).
Week 2–3: SLO drafting workshops with service owners (Sofia + Priya).
Week 4: runbook pairing sessions, Confluence templates finalized (Benji).
Week 5–7: engineering sprints for gating + alerting (Ethan + Marcus).
Week 8–10: pilot monitoring, threshold tuning, runbook dry runs.
Week 11–12: training, cutover, retrospective and org-wide roll plan.

Appendix A — Quick policy matrix (summary):
- Green (budget > 50%): normal ops.
- Yellow (budget 20%–50%): reduced risk deploys only, increase monitoring cadence.
- Red (budget < 20%): block auto-promotions, notify product and oncall, consider traffic shaping.

Appendix B — Useful links and templates:
- SLO template: confluence.redwood.local/reliability/slo-template
- Runbook template: confluence.redwood.local/reliability/runbook-template
- PagerDuty taxonomy doc: confluence.redwood.local/tools/pagerduty-taxonomy

Notes to reviewers:
- Please comment inline on the SLO thresholds and the CI gating proposal.
- If your team wants to be added to the pilot, ping me (Aisha) with owner name and SLI coverage by EOD next Friday.
